When we cut the Thames Valley region by local
authority, Milton Keynes comes out as the most
populous area of high-growth companies. Most of
these businesses are operating within business
and professional services, including
Software-as-a-Service and marketing tools.

Oxford is the next most populous area, playing
host to 166 high-growth companies, 66 of which
are academic spinouts. It’s no surprise then, that
many of the companies are operating across
pharmaceuticals, research tools and reagents and
artificial intelligence.

Spinout stats.

Unsurprisingly the University of Oxford is
responsible for the majority of the spinouts in
the Thames Valley, having spun out
companies since 2011.

Perhaps the most notable of these is unicorn
company Oxford Nanopore, which develops a
range of portable DNA and RNA sequencing
devices, that are also capable of characterising
epigenetic modifications.

The Science and Technology Facilities Council is
responsible for 6 spinouts in the Thames Valley,
as is Imperial College.

Impact of COVID-19

The impact of COVID-19 on Thames Valley
businesses is akin to the wider country, with
around half of companies experiencing a low or
potentially positive impact, and just over a third
seeing a moderate impact. 15% are at severe or
critical risk, and will need additional support to
make it through the pandemic.

The 154 Thames Valley businesses operating
within the medical and life sciences sectors,
including Oxford Nanopore and Immunocore, are
far less likely to be negatively affected—just 27%
are facing moderate to critical risk. Another 22%
are likely to experience a positive impact.
